title: Spotfix owner queue & compact coverage
body:
Purpose: compact, scannable owner queue for ad-hoc spotfixes (weekend spike / cross-regional fallbacks). Lightweight single-sheet view so oncall/rotations and SEs can grab ownership quickly.

Guiding principles (quick):
- single owner per area where possible (no split ownership unless paired)
- explicit fallback contact + 30 min SLA to respond for critical endpoints
- short ETA estimates only (0.5h / 2h / 4h buckets) to guide routing
- mark manual intervention steps clearly so SRE knows when to escalate to infra

Snapshot (last updated 2028-03-15 09:10 PT)

Area | Current owner | Fallback | Priority | Est to triage | Est to resolve | Current status | Quick notes
edge-router / ingress | Jonah Reed | Pager: infra-rotations | P0 | 0.5h | 2h | monitoring alerted, throttled 10% | prefix-cache warm in progress; watch refcount
model-serving v2 | Marta Liu | Diego Alvarez | P0/P1 mixed | 1h | 4h | slow tail-latency on long sequences | temporary q8 fallback enabled; metric: token-latency p95 up 180ms
embeddings API | unassigned | SE oncall (rot) | P1 | 2h | 4h | elevated errors 502 | suspect mem pressure on dedicated pools
dedicated-gpu-burst | Diego Alvarez | Jonah Reed | P1 | 1h | 6h | capacity trembling during US morning | autoscale policy flagged; manual burst enabled
console-rollouts | Aisha Patel | Product-ops channel | P2 | 4h | N/A | partial dashboard gaps | missing trace sampling for route /api/v1/generate
cross-region-fallback | Marta Liu | global-oncall | P0 | 0.5h | 1h | successful failover test yesterday | ensure route weights adjusted for eu-west-2

Quick counts
- total areas tracked: 6
- unassigned owners: 1 (embeddings API)
- P0 items: 3 (edge-router, model-serving v2, cross-region-fallback)
- Estimated overall triage headroom: ~3.5 hours of immediate ops availability across oncall

Immediate actions (who / when)
1) assign embeddings API owner before EOD (Aisha) — due 2028-03-15 17:00 PT. Reason: reduce double-handoffs for 502s.
2) Jonah to confirm prefix-cache stabilization + post a short note in #prod-coverage (Jonah) — due 2028-03-15 10:00 PT.
3) Marta to run a focused p95 tail-run for model-serving v2 with sequence length 4096 sample (Marta) — due 2028-03-15 12:00 PT. Link results to JIRA OPS-4829.
4) Diego to validate dedicated-gpu-burst autoscale thresholds and create short rollback play if manual burst costs escalate (Diego) — due 2028-03-15 13:30 PT.

Playbook snippets (copy/paste for oncall)
- If edge-router has >15% throttle rate: add prefix-cache node (run scripts/edge/add-cache.sh), notify infra, pin traffic weights to 0.8 for static routes.
- If model-serving v2 tail p95 > target + 150ms: switch to q4 quantized variant for canary traffic (console -> rollout -> instant fallback), file regression tag in RDW-evals.
- Embeddings 502 pattern: check pool OOM logs (k8s events), rotate pool, restart pool controllers; if persists, escalate to platform-engineering.

Open questions / rough TODOs
- Do we want a two-tier SLA (critical endpoints 30m, non-critical 90m) explicitly in this sheet? (proposal: yes, see item for Product-ops policy)
- Should SEs be assigned as fallback for embeddings for next 48h? Pros: faster domain knowledge. Cons: disrupts SE schedule. (Marta to advise)
- Can we automate owner assignment for low-priority items by mapping service tags -> team rota? Low effort prototype: map via /ops/rotas.csv and a simple Lambda. (Diego)

Notes to self (Aisha)
- keep this compact; stakeholders consume quick lines not prose.
- if this becomes >8 areas, split into 'critical' and 'secondary' sheets to avoid noise.
- link to longer incident postmortem if one arises (CONFLUENCE:RDW-ops-incident-templates).

Revision history
- 2028-03-07 created (initial quick roster)
- 2028-03-10 updated: added dedicated-gpu-burst row after morning spike
- 2028-03-15 updated: set priorities, added plays + assigned action owners

Contact for questions: Aisha Patel (aisha@redwood.ai) — if offline, ping Diego or Jonah in #prod-coverage.

Raw export notes: this sheet was originally assembled from quick Slack signals, Datadog alerts, and an ad-hoc k8s pod list. Intentionally minimal formatting to keep copy/paste friendly for phone viewing.
